speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with gait and limb ataxia; to begin my assessment, could you please describe exactly how your unsteadiness started and if you have any specific medical history related to your neurological, endocrine, or oncological health?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description, Mr. Patient. You mentioned feeling clumsy specifically on the right side; does this unsteadiness worsen when you look to the right, or does it persist regardless of gaze? Additionally, do you have any history of diabetes or recent infections?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a very significant detail, Mr. Patient. Given your history of Crohn's disease and use of natalizumab, are you experiencing any new visual disturbances, such as double vision or trouble focusing? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast; REQUEST TEST: JC virus antibody test.

text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)

The MRI findings showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, combined with your history of natalizumab use for Crohn's disease, are diagnostic for PML caused by reactivation of the JC virus. MS is unlikely given the specific imaging pattern and your medication history.
